title: Perception of Color in Architecture and Urban Space
research_question: To examine the role of color in the composition of urban space as an element affecting observers and to explore how color can support architecture and urban space, and what effects can be achieved through its intended use.

participants.description: Final-year students at the Faculty of Architecture (two successive years) in Wrocław, Poland.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: 18 photographic views of architecture in various urban contexts, locations, seasons, weather conditions, and lighting. Each photo featured a dominant, distinctive, or eye-catching color or group of colors, sometimes with patterns, from facade finishes or natural materials.

measures.construct: Perception of color composition harmony/integration vs. disturbance
measures.instrument: 5-point Likert scale (1 = 'harmonious and integrating', 5 = 'intrusive and disturbing')

findings.antecedent: Red color in window recesses and sills of brick buildings in Nikiszowiec (historic working-class housing estate), combined with natural red shade of brick (67% rated 1, 19.3% rated 2).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as very harmonious and integrating with surroundings.
findings.mechanism: Historical and cultural value, harmonious combination of distinctive red with natural brick shade, traditional local material.
findings.quote: students chose as one of the most harmonious color compositions... red color appears here as a historical and cultural value

findings.antecedent: Ephemeral color and light installation with delicate, pastel colors (pink, turquoise, orange) on semi-transparent textile ribbons/voiles suspended above a commercial passage (67% rated 1, 14.8% rated 2).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as very harmonious, pleasant, and creating a gentle, festive mood.
findings.mechanism: Creates a more human scale, lightness, translucency, illumination, gentle/festive mood, meets emotional expectations.
findings.quote: The positively assessed color composition is here an element that complements the urban space... promotes satisfaction

findings.antecedent: Lively, pastel colors on Victorian row houses in San Francisco's Haight-Ashbury district, with decorative details (52.3% rated 1, 26.1% rated 2).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as harmoniously fitting into the spatial context and representing historical and cultural value.
findings.mechanism: Associated with the identity of the place, its history and culture, impressive color composition.
findings.quote: The impressive color composition of Victorian buildings... appear here as a historical and cultural value

findings.antecedent: Warm brownish colors of modern high-rise Encore and Wynn hotels in Las Vegas, with shiny glass facades resembling copper sheets, chameleon-like color changing subtly with sky/weather (35.2% rated 1, 34.1% rated 2).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as harmonizing with the grays of the cloudy sky and beige of classic architecture, making buildings recognizable and memorable.
findings.mechanism: Harmonizes with surrounding colors, distinguishes buildings in Las Vegas, makes them recognizable and memorable as landmarks.
findings.quote: The warm brownish colors of the modern architecture... harmonize with both the grays of the cloudy sky

findings.antecedent: Hand-painted murals in colors representing lush greenery of Florida on Swan and Dolphin Hotels at Walt Disney World Resort (29.5% rated 1, 28.4% rated 2).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as highly harmonizing with the surroundings and matching the fairy-tale image of Disneyland.
findings.mechanism: Matches fairy-tale image, complements tropical landscape, element of entertainment and fun.
findings.quote: highly rated in terms of colors harmonizing with the surroundings. The characteristic architecture... matches the fairy-tale image

findings.antecedent: Two-tone 'layered' facade of Data Center office building in Toronto, with reddish textured ceramic 'baguette' panels alluding to historic clay brick architecture (25% rated 1, 38.6% rated 2).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as harmoniously referring to the environment context and representing historical/cultural value.
findings.mechanism: Alludes to rich local context of clay brick architecture, pays tribute to historic buildings and contemporary architecture.
findings.quote: recognized by the students as harmoniously referring to the environment context

findings.antecedent: Pink-tinted insulating glass dome with turquoise-pink spatial frame covering Adventuredome Indoor Theme Park in Las Vegas (13.6% rated 1, 18.2% rated 2, 19.3% rated 3, 19.3% rated 4, 5.7% rated 5).
findings.consequent: Perception of color scheme as harmonious and consistent with entertainment architecture and theme parks.
findings.mechanism: Closely related to the function of the building, consistent with entertainment architecture and theme parks.
findings.quote: The color scheme, closely related to the function of the building, was positively assessed by students

findings.antecedent: Dominant expressive orange color on upper part of Angel City apartment building in Wrocław, contrasting with neutral white and gray historical/modern buildings, complemented by autumn tree colors (36.4% rated 1, 30.7% rated 2).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as harmonious, despite the orange color being quite aggressive.
findings.mechanism: Complements building's color scheme via saturation contrast, temperature contrast (warm orange vs. cold white/gray), and harmonizes with autumn tree colors.
findings.quote: the students assessed this color composition as harmonious. Although the color itself is quite aggressive, it complements

findings.antecedent: White color of archdiocesan library architecture as an accent against reddish bricks, yellowish plaster, green patina on copper roofs, and red ceramic tiles of historic buildings in Ostrów Tumski, Wrocław (36.4% rated 1, 29.5% rated 2).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as harmonious, complementing and exposing the historic urban space.
findings.mechanism: Complements and exposes historic urban space, brightness contrast (white reduces brightness of other colors), temperature contrast (cold white against warm reds/yellows), favorable landscape/weather conditions.
findings.quote: The discussed color composition complements and exposes the historic urban space on the basis of the new building's whiteness

findings.antecedent: Dynamic, high-contrast, aggressive color composition of dark black metal divided by bright red ribs on International Spy Museum building in Washington D.C., surrounded by older buildings (34.1% rated 3, 26.1% rated 4, 22.7% rated 5).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as disharmonious, imposing, disturbing, and interfering with urban space.
findings.mechanism: Extreme contrasting colors, strongly emphasized forms (slanted/sharp), large scale, non-static/dynamic composition, causing mental tension/unpleasantness.
findings.quote: critical assessment of the students strongly indicated the imposing, disturbing and interfering color scheme

findings.antecedent: Dominant intense red paint covering a modern multi-family residential building (Nowa Manufaktura) in Wrocław, contrasting with dark graphite and white, and smaller-scale neighboring historic tenement houses (35.2% rated 4, 29.5% rated 5).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as dissonant, intrusive, undesirable, and causing mental tension, anxiety, irritability.
findings.mechanism: Dominance of red, extreme color contrast, adds heaviness, intensifies stylistic chaos, causes mental tension/discomfort.
findings.quote: Students negatively assessed the color dissonance of this composition, resulting primarily from the dominance of red

findings.antecedent: Intense red facade of Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science building in Wrocław, contrasting with blue paint on Grunwaldzki Bridge and white facade of neighboring residential building, in cloudy winter conditions (43.2% rated 4, 19.3% rated 5).
findings.consequent: Perception of color composition as dissonant, irritating, unnatural, and 'out of place'.
findings.mechanism: Red perceived as too different/contrasting, weather conditions (cloudy sky, lack of sunlight) emphasize expressiveness of red, making it irritating.
findings.quote: the red color of architecture is perceived as irritating, unnatural and “out of place”.

findings.antecedent: Multicolor, graphic, and visual contrast of black and white pixelated 'Dalmatian dog skin' superstructure resting on 12 colorful slanted legs (some black) of Sharp Center for Design, OCAD University, Toronto (23.9% rated 2, 26.1% rated 3, 29.5% rated 4).
findings.consequent: Mixed perception of color composition harmony, likely due to expressiveness and use of diverse, vivid colors against a subdued neighborhood.
findings.mechanism: Expressiveness and diverse, vivid colors against subdued background, extreme color contrasts, dynamism of body and form, stylistic diversity.
findings.quote: The discrepancy in the assessment of this color composition... may rather result from its expressiveness

findings.antecedent: Clearly 'candy' shade pink facade of a dog rescue and adoption home in Beverly Hills, including details, with intense blue cafe elements (22.7% rated 1, 21.6% rated 2, 20.5% rated 3, 20.5% rated 4, 14.8% rated 5).
findings.consequent: Strongly divided opinions on color composition harmony, with some finding it balancing on the verge of kitsch, others finding it emphasizing character and fitting context.
findings.mechanism: Pink color partly results from building's purpose ('palace for puppies'), emphasizes character, fits context, but can be perceived as infantile/kitsch.
findings.quote: students' opinions in this case were strongly divided. The pink color may partly result from the purpose of the building

findings.antecedent: Eye-catching intense blue Prismatic Blue coating in entrance area of Ryerson University Student Learning Center, contrasting with milky gray patterned glass facades (15.9% rated 1, 22.7% rated 2, 38.6% rated 3).
findings.consequent: Mixed perception of color composition harmony, with opinions more oriented towards positive evaluation, but not unanimously harmonious.
findings.mechanism: Expressiveness of building emphasized by color scheme, stands out against surroundings, cool/contrasting colors, strongly emphasized forms, large scale, non-static/dynamic composition.
findings.quote: opinion was more oriented towards a positive evaluation. This is the only night shot included in the survey.

findings.antecedent: Dynamic purple lighting of 'Spodek' sports and entertainment hall in Katowice at night, with new scales of light pearl gray aluminum (12.5% rated 1, 27% rated 2, 33% rated 3).
findings.consequent: Mixed perception of color composition harmony, with opinions more oriented towards positive evaluation, but not unanimously harmonious.
findings.mechanism: Purple lighting likely influenced assessment; designers did not consider appropriate arrangement/intensity of light, causing object to lose materiality, creating safety hazard, light pollution.
findings.quote: The purple color of the building's lighting captured in the photo most likely influenced the students' assessment.

findings.antecedent: Dominant blue facade of Galeria Skarbek in Katowice, with strip horizontal divisions, contrasting with subdued red roofs, facade bricks, and gray pavement, in winter morning light (39.8% rated 3, 22.7% rated 4, 14.8% rated 5).
findings.consequent: Mixed perception of color composition harmony, with the vast majority finding it disharmonious.
findings.mechanism: Low score due to winter photo lacking green trees, morning light cooling atmosphere and emphasizing cold blue, subduing red shades.
findings.quote: the vast majority of students found it disharmonious... photo was taken in the winter, lacking green trees

mechanisms: Historical and cultural value of color
Emotional impact (mental tension, relaxation, joy, irritation, feeling overwhelmed)
Cognitive effects (recognition, memorability, orientation, legibility, confusion)
Aesthetic principles (color harmony, contrast, saturation, brightness, temperature contrast, proportions, scale, form, texture)
Contextual fit (surroundings, function, season, time of day, weather, natural lighting)
Psychophysical structure and personal characteristics influencing color preferences
moderators: Personal characteristics (age, gender, ethnicity, culture, type of work, knowledge, experience)
Time (season, time of day, weather conditions)
implementation_implications: Supplement architectural education programs with broadly understood knowledge about color and its impact on humans.
Encourage students to observe nature as the most important form of teaching about colors and aesthetics.

Thoughtful, conscious use of color can achieve specific effects in urban space, supporting functions, readability, aesthetic value, symbolic value, contrast/integration, homogeneity, distinguishing/merging, attractiveness, camouflage.

Color treatments can include distinguishing/emphasizing objects, highlighting forms, emphasizing rhythms/divisions/elements, merging/splitting structures, visual changes in size/proportions, counteracting monotony, giving dynamic character, bonding/integrating forms, matching colors for harmony/order, creating optical illusions/surprise/camouflage, and introducing various color contrasts.

tables.description: Presentation of 18 pictures of architecture in urban contexts and evaluation results showing the percentage of students who rated each picture on a 5-point scale (1=harmonious/integrating, 5=intrusive/disturbing).
key_stats: Photo 9: 22.7% rated 1, 21.6% rated 2, 20.5% rated 3, 20.5% rated 4, 14.8% rated 5

limitations: Difficulty and ambiguity in predicting color aesthetics due to individual perception and experience.
Students' perceptions could be related to their previous experiences and knowledge of specific examples of architecture, as photo locations were not indicated.
Possible insufficient knowledge among students regarding socio-economic conditions influencing post-war architecture (for photo 14).
Not all students may have considered factors like light arrangement, safety hazards, or light pollution in their assessment of dynamic lighting (for photo 15).

paper_metadata.title: Perception of Color in Architecture and Urban Space
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Perception of Color in Architecture and Urban Space
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: The various colors and color combinations in an urban environment are perceived and experienced individually. The article indicates the important role of color in shaping architecture and urban space. The paper discusses the theories of color harmony as an aesthetic principle in architectural design. The results of the research have proven the significant role of color as an element of the composition of urban space affecting the observer. This translates into the importance of color in architectural design, taking into account the difficulty and ambiguity in predicting color aesthetics; the impact of color on humans; and its cognitive, emotional and behavioral effects. The information and conclusions obtained as a result of the literature studies and the results of the survey gave the basis for determining various color strategies in shaping architecture and the effects that we can achieve in urban space thanks to a well-thought-out, conscious use of colors. The research findings also indicate that it is necessary to supplement architectural education programs with broadly understood knowledge about color and its impact on humans. The implemented activities are a response to current ideas and directions in designing and teaching architectural design outlined and suggested as part of the New European Bauhaus initiative.
